newsitem.title: INDIA: India forms committee to resolve airport row.
newsitem.headline: India forms committee to resolve airport row.

text.p: India said on Thursday it had set up a committee to resolve differences between the Civil Aviation Ministry and private investors over a proposed $335 million international airport project near Bangalore.

Civil Aviation Minister Chand Mahal Ibrahim held discussions on Thursday with Ratan Tata, chairman of India's Tata group, which is involved in the project with U.S.-based Raytheon Company and Singapore's Changi Airport Authority.

"While many issues relating to the project were resolved, there was difference in perception with regard to the concept of build, own and operate (BOO) and build, operate and transfer (BOT) and certain other issues," the ministry said in a statement.

The panel, headed by Ranjan Chatterjee, chairman of the state-run Airport Authority of India, will comprise members from the federal government, government of the state of Karnataka and India's Tata group, it said.
Bangalore is the capital of Karnataka, whose government has criticised Ibrahim for shifting New Delhi's position on the project.
Indian authorities had originally negotiated the project on a BOO basis. But Ibrahim now says the private consortium must transfer the airport project to the government on a BOT basis.
He said earlier this week that the project would be handed over to the state-run Airports Authority of India if the Tatas did not agree to his condition.
The panel has been asked to submit a report within 20 days, the statement said.
India invited foreign investors to build airports or other infrastructural facilities under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
